challenges.title: Encoding Matryoshka
challenges.description:
A doll inside a doll inside a doll. Three layers, all of them reversible encodings, none of them encryption.

The file tells you which layer comes next if you look at the alphabet.

**Goal:** unwrap all three layers.

hints.text: Binary → decimal → hex → base64 is a reasonable first guess.
Every layer has a fingerprint: fixed block lengths, `=` padding, a restricted alphabet. Identify one, decode, repeat.

challenges.title: Python Golf
challenges.description:
Eleven lines of aggressively golfed Python. It takes a string and returns `True` only for the flag.

**Goal:** reverse the logic and recover the input. Running it with guesses is allowed but slow.

hints.text: Rewrite it with real variable names. The obfuscation is cosmetic.
It checks pairs of characters against a rolling hash. Solve backwards from the known prefix `SNT{`.

challenges.title: Regex Rumble
challenges.description:
A log file where exactly one line matches all six conditions listed in the attached rule sheet. The others match five.

**Goal:** write the regex, extract the token, submit it as the flag. No guessing — the rules are precise.

hints.text: Use lookaheads, or filter progressively with grep and check what survives.
The IP must be in 10.0.0.0/8 but not 10.0.1.0/24, and the status must not be 200.

challenges.title: Hash Hunt
challenges.description:
`SHA-256("SNT{" + word + "}") == 6f3c...` — and the word is a six-letter lowercase English word.

**Goal:** recover the word. A wordlist and ten lines of Python beat a GPU you do not have.

hints.text: `rockyou.txt` has it. `hashcat -m 1400` works if you prefer.
The word starts with 's' and is security-adjacent.

challenges.title: Esolang Detour
challenges.description:
The challenge is a single line of punctuation. It is a valid Brainfuck program that prints exactly one string: the flag.

**Goal:** run it (mentally or otherwise) and read the output. Then explain why the tape has 30,000 cells.

hints.text: Any Brainfuck interpreter will do — or write twelve lines of Python.
If you want to solve it statically, note that every run of `+` before a `.` is one character.
